info.name: GenLink KH — Backend API
info.description:
GenLink KH backend (Spring Boot, port 8888).

## Quick start
1. Set the `baseUrl` variable if your server is not on http://localhost:8888.
2. Run **Auth > Register**, then **Auth > Verify Email** with the 6-digit OTP.
   The OTP is printed to the backend console (`EMAIL OTP FOR ...`), which is handy
   because SMTP may not be configured.
3. Or just run **Auth > Login** if you already have an account.

Login, Verify Email, Verify OTP and the Refresh requests all capture
`accessToken` and `refreshToken` into collection variables automatically, so
every other request is authenticated for you.

## Notes
- All responses are wrapped: `{ success, message, data, errorCode, timestamp }`.
- Auth is Bearer JWT, set once at collection level. Public endpoints override it to none.
- Access tokens last 15 minutes and carry a `tv` (token version) claim. Logout,
  change-password and revoke-all bump it, so the token dies immediately — that is
  intended, just log in again.
- `Accept-Language: km` or `en` controls the language of system content such as
  interest names. Default is Khmer.

item.name: Media
item.description:
Presigned direct upload to S3-compatible object storage (DigitalOcean Spaces).

The backend never handles the bytes: it signs, validates and records. Run the requests in order 1 -> 2 -> 3.

STEP 1 needs the file's SHA-256 and byte size. On Windows PowerShell:
  (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 'C:\path\test.jpg').Hash.ToLower()
  (Get-Item 'C:\path\test.jpg').Length
Put those into the mediaChecksum and mediaSizeBytes collection variables.

STEP 2 goes to DigitalOcean, NOT to this API. It is pre-authorised by the signed URL, so Authorization must be off and the Content-Type header must match exactly what was presigned.

request.description:
Validates mime + size for the purpose, reserves an object key, writes a PENDING row and returns a presigned PUT URL (valid 5 min).

purpose: AVATAR | POST | STORY | SHORT | EVENT_COVER | COMMUNITY_COVER | PORTFOLIO
Video is only allowed for STORY and SHORT.
Caps: 5 MB image, 50 MB video - re-enforced at confirm against the real size.
checksumSha256 must be 64 lowercase hex characters.

Goes straight to DigitalOcean Spaces - NOT to this API.

BEFORE SENDING: open the Body tab, choose 'binary', and Select File. Postman cannot script the file choice, so an unselected body uploads 0 bytes and confirm then rejects it with MEDIA_EMPTY.

Authorization is off on purpose: the presigned URL carries its own. Leaving a Bearer token on it breaks the signature.

Content-Type must equal the contentType sent to presign, with no charset suffix, or Spaces answers 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.

Expect 200 with an empty body.

exec: pm.test('object is not empty', function () { pm.expect(d.sizeBytes).to.be.above(0); });

request.description:
HEADs the object to confirm it exists and to read its real size and LastModified, stores the dimensions you pass, grants public-read, and returns the CDN url.

width/height/durationMs come from the client's local file - the backend never reads the bytes. Send null for whatever does not apply.

Errors: MEDIA_NOT_UPLOADED (no object), MEDIA_EMPTY (0 bytes - the file was not attached in step 2), MEDIA_ALREADY_CONFIRMED, MEDIA_TOO_LARGE.
Public media returns its stable CDN url; private media returns a short-lived presigned GET. Only the owner may mint a private url.

Soft delete: stamps deleted_at and hides the media. The bytes stay in the bucket until MediaCleanupJob purges them after the 30-day retention window, so a mistaken delete is recoverable until then. Owner only.
Proves the server enforces the size cap regardless of any client-side compression.

request.description:
Password step of admin sign-in (ADM-021, SSOT 8.1).

Answers 401 + ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED on SUCCESS, carrying a 5-minute challenge token in `data`. The caller is not authenticated yet, so 401 is correct; the errorCode is what distinguishes 'finish signing in' from 'wrong credentials'.

The challenge token authenticates nothing - its `typ` claim matches no route. Only /admin/auth/mfa/verify accepts it (ADM-023).

Every rejection - wrong password, unknown email, a user who is not an admin, a revoked admin - returns an identical 401 UNAUTHORIZED body, deliberately: anything else would reveal which accounts are administrators.

Rate limited on a dedicated ADMIN_LOGIN bucket: 5 failures / 15 min, then a 15-minute block returning 429 RATE_LIMITED.

request.description:
Reissues the ten recovery codes and INVALIDATES EVERY PREVIOUS ONE - spent or not. An admin still holding old codes on paper must discard them.

Requires an open sudo window: send 'Sudo' first, or this answers 403 ADMIN_SUDO_REQUIRED. A fresh set is a permanent bypass of the second factor, so a live session alone is not enough to mint one.

This is the path back for an admin who has spent all ten codes - without it the only remedy is an MFA reset by someone with rbac:manage, which for a lone SUPER_ADMIN means database access.

Shown once. Stored BCrypt-hashed.

item.description:
Admin portal authentication (SSOT 8.1). Runs end to end with no copy-paste.

SET FIRST: {{adminEmail}}, {{adminPassword}}.

FIRST-TIME ADMIN (never enrolled) - run in order:
  1. Admin Login            -> captures {{adminChallengeToken}}
  2. MFA Enrol              -> captures {{adminTotpSecret}}, prints the otpauth:// URI
  3. MFA Confirm            -> code auto-generated; returns 10 recovery codes. SAVE THEM.
  4. MFA Verify             -> captures {{adminAccessToken}} + {{adminRefreshToken}}
  5. Me                     -> identity + resolved permissions
The challenge lives 5 minutes. If steps 2-4 take longer, re-run Admin Login.

ALREADY-ENROLLED ADMIN - the normal case:
  1. Admin Login   2. MFA Verify   3. Me
MFA Enrol will refuse with ADMIN_MFA_ALREADY_ENROLLED, which is correct.

  For the code to be auto-generated you need {{adminTotpSecret}} set. It is
  returned exactly once, at enrolment, so if you enrolled elsewhere paste it in
  by hand ONCE - that is setup, not per-request copy-paste. Otherwise replace
  {{adminTotpCode}} in the body with a code from your authenticator.

HOW THE CODE IS GENERATED
  A pre-request script on Confirm / Verify / Sudo computes RFC 6238 TOTP from
  {{adminTotpSecret}} using crypto-js. It was verified against the RFC 6238
  Appendix B vectors before being committed.

SUDO-GATED REQUESTS
  'Regenerate recovery codes' answers 403 ADMIN_SUDO_REQUIRED until you run
  'Sudo'. That 403 is worth seeing once - it is the control that bounds what an
  unattended, unlocked laptop can do (SSOT 10.7).

WHAT THE STATUS CODES MEAN HERE
  Admin Login answers 401 ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED on SUCCESS. The caller is not
  authenticated yet - they hold a challenge, which grants nothing on its own.

item.name: Admin Dashboard
item.description: Read-only Phase 2 dashboard aggregates. Run Admin Auth first and set {{adminAccessToken}}. Each section may be null when its backing aggregate is unavailable (ADM-045). DAU/MAU are estimated proxy metrics (ADM-046): successful login events and refresh-token activity are de-duplicated by user and bucketed in Asia/Phnom_Penh.

request.description: Requires dashboard:view. Returns seven KPI cards, 90-day user growth, 30-day registrations, estimated DAU/MAU activity, account status split, recent admin actions and recent registrations. DAU/MAU count each user once per day/rolling 30-day window across successful login and refresh-token activity. Date buckets use Asia/Phnom_Penh.

Requires dashboard:view and an enrolled admin access token. Returns normalized UP/DEGRADED/DOWN status for API, PostgreSQL and storage, plus mail SUCCESS/FAILURE/NEVER_RUN and the three scheduled-job last-run states. No credentials, URLs, bucket names or raw exceptions are returned.

Requires user:read. Returns active, non-expired, non-revoked refresh-token session metadata for {{adminUserId}}. Token hashes are never returned.

Requires user:read. Returns newest-first security audit events for {{adminUserId}} with event type, outcome, failure reason, IP, user agent and timestamp. Audit details, email and credentials are not returned.
Requires user:read. Returns total XP, level progress, source breakdown, signed newest-first XP ledger and earned badges for {{adminUserId}}.

Marks the request REMOVED without counting the user. The person may request again later, which re-opens a PENDING request. Owner/admin only.

Promote/demote a member. role: ADMIN | MODERATOR | MEMBER (OWNER is rejected — use Transfer Ownership).

Owner or admin only; an admin may only manage MODERATOR and MEMBER, never another admin or the owner. You cannot change your own role. Non-managers get 404.
